text: dsh-ip-based-acl 是一个 DSH Web 插件 bundle：它在 Harness 的 Host row 中接入 connection 服务，并按配置的 IP 地址或 CIDR allowlist 判断 Web 请求是否可用。插件解析 IPv4、IPv6 及映射地址，支持配置受信代理后按 X-Forwarded-For 链识别客户端，并将访问判断应用于页面、请求接纳和连接认证入口。适合希望按网络来源划定 DSH Web 可访问范围的部署。配置项为 allow 与 trustedProxies；不需要 API key 或外部账号。

dsh-ip-based-acl is a DSH web bundle that checks client IP and CIDR rules at the Harness connection entry points. It supports IPv4, IPv6, and trusted proxy address chains. Configure allow and trustedProxies; no API key or external account is required.
我想只让指定 IP 网段访问 DSH 的网页界面。
DSH Web 能按 IPv4 或 IPv6 地址限制访问吗？
让反向代理后面的 DSH 服务根据真实客户端 IP 放行。
有没有办法把网络来源检查加到 DSH 页面和接口入口？
Can I restrict the DSH web interface to specific IP ranges?
How can my DSH server identify allowed clients behind trusted proxies?
dsh-ip-based-acl 的功能「IP 与 CIDR allowlist」：根据配置的 IPv4 或 IPv6 地址及网段判断客户端是否可访问 DSH Web；在 profile 的 allow 中填写规则。
dsh-ip-based-acl 的功能「受信代理客户端识别」：配置 trustedProxies 后，根据代理的 X-Forwarded-For 地址链解析客户端 IP；直接连接时使用 socket 对端地址。
dsh-ip-based-acl 的功能「Web 请求入口接入」：bundle 启用 Host row 后，在页面授权、请求接纳和连接授权入口应用地址判断；允许的客户端继续调用原入口。
dsh-ip-based-acl README · dsh-ip-based-acl：A DeepSeek Harness plugin bundle that gates the Harness web surface by peer IP address.

dsh-ip-based-acl README · dsh-ip-based-acl：> [!WARNING]
> **Early project, not security-reviewed.** This is 0.1.x: the tests drive a stub Connection, the gate
> has never run against a live Harness, and nobody has audited it. Treat it as an experiment that
> works in the cases it tests, not as a boundary you can rely on — an address allowlist is one layer,
> never a substitute for a firewall, a TLS-terminating proxy, or a VPN.
>
> **Do not expose DSH to the internet.** The Harness is powerful by design: it drives an agent with
> access to the machine it runs on, able to read and write files, execute commands, and reach the
> network. An instance reachable by someone you did not intend is, for practical purposes, remote code
> execution on that host. This bundle decides which peer addresses reach the door; it does not make
> public exposure safe. Misconfiguration cuts both ways: an empty `allow` locks everyone out, and a
> `trustedProxies` entry that covers real clients lets a forged `X-Forwarded-For` through. Run it on
> loopback or behind a private network — VPN, WireGuard, Tailscale, an SSH tunnel — and keep it off the
> public internet.

dsh-ip-based-acl README · dsh-ip-based-acl：Status: **implemented, not installed**. The allowlist is compiled at activation and installed as a
gate over Connection's admission, index, and connect entries, with `X-Forwarded-For` resolution
through configured proxies. The bundle has not been installed into a live profile, so the gate has
not yet been exercised against a running Harness.

dsh-ip-based-acl README · Install：Node 24 or newer and pnpm are enough to build and test it: Cordis resolves from the Harness that loads
the bundle at runtime, and from `devDependencies` for the local checks. `lib/` is generated rather than
committed, so build before installing:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/arinanto/dsh-ip-based-acl.git
cd dsh-ip-based-acl
pnpm install
pnpm build

dsh-ip-based-acl README · Install：Install that directory as a **bundle** in a DSH profile — the Harness Plugin Manager's install action,
or the `plugin_manager` tool with `action: install_bundle` and the checkout's absolute path as
`target`. It contributes one Host row, `ip-based-acl`, and ships it without config.

Configure `allow` **before enabling the row**: the default is deny-everything, loopback included, so a
row enabled with an empty list makes the web interface unreachable until you edit the profile patch and
restart.

dsh-ip-based-acl README · Install：```yaml
- id: ip-based-acl
  config:
    allow: ["127.0.0.1", "::1"]
    trustedProxies: []

A manual install is the same package link the Plugin Manager makes:
`dsh plugin --profile <name> add <path-to-this-checkout>`, which forwards `pnpm add` inside the profile.

dsh-ip-based-acl README · Policy：- A client is admitted only when its address sits inside a configured address or CIDR network. A bare
  address is a single-host rule (`203.0.113.9` is `/32`, `::1` is `/128`).
- A client that matches no entry is refused with `403`, even when it presents a valid launch token or
  an existing session cookie.
- An empty `allow` list refuses every client, loopback included, and logs a warning at activation.
- A missing or unparseable client address is refused, never treated as local.
- A malformed pattern fails activation, so a typo cannot become a silent grant.
- IPv4 and IPv6 share one 128-bit space: `10.0.0.0/8` and `::ffff:10.0.0.0/104` describe the same
  peers, and a mapped peer matches either spelling.
- Loopback must be listed explicitly (`127.0.0.1` and/or `::1`). A dual-stack listener often reports
  an IPv4 peer in mapped form (`::ffff:127.0.0.1`), which the IPv4 rule already covers.

dsh-ip-based-acl README · Proxies：`trustedProxies` names the reverse proxies whose `X-Forwarded-For` header may be believed. The chain
is resolved with [MDN's trusted-proxy-list method](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/X-Forwarded-For#trusted_proxy_list):

dsh-ip-based-acl README · Proxies：- The socket peer is authoritative. If it is not in `trustedProxies`, it is the client and the header
  is ignored entirely — a direct client cannot spoof its way in.
- If it is, the list is read right to left, starting with the address the nearest proxy recorded and
  skipping every entry that is itself a trusted proxy. The first entry that is not one is the client.
  It may be an untrusted intermediate proxy rather than the origin, but it is the only address fit
  for an access decision.
- Repeated `X-Forwarded-For` headers form one chain. A malformed entry is treated as the client and
  therefore refused.
- Name only proxies you control, never a client subnet: any host inside a trusted range can forge the
  header. A trusted proxy that sends no header falls back to its own address, so do not list a proxy
  in `allow` unless requests resolving to it should be admitted.
- The proxy must add `X-Forwarded-For` to the WebSocket upgrade as well as to plain HTTP requests.
  An upgrade that arrives without it resolves to the proxy's own address.
- An empty `trustedProxies` ignores the header, which is the safe default for a directly exposed
  server.

dsh-ip-based-acl README · Proxies：```yaml
- id: ip-based-acl
  config:
    allow: ["203.0.113.7", "127.0.0.1", "::1"]
    trustedProxies: ["10.0.0.1"]

dsh-ip-based-acl README · Enforcement：The web carrier has no pre-dispatch hook and Connection exposes no policy extension point, so the
gate wraps the three entry points that decide whether a browser may use the interface:

dsh-ip-based-acl README · Enforcement：| Entry point                   | Covers                                                                                                          |
| ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `connection.admit`            | every credential-bearing request: `/api`, the Remote-stream WebSocket, and feature routes using `requestRejection` |
| `connection.authorizeIndex`   | the page itself and the launch-token exchange                                                                   |
| `connection.authorizeConnect` | the API credential exchange on `/connect`                                                                       |

dsh-ip-based-acl README · Enforcement：An admitted peer continues through the normal token and cookie flow unchanged. A refused peer is
answered before Connection reads the credential, so no token is exchanged, no cookie is minted, and a
cookie issued earlier buys nothing. Disposal restores every original method.

Scope limits, stated plainly:

dsh-ip-based-acl README · Enforcement：- Public asset routes (plugin bundles, HMR events) stay reachable; they carry no session data, and
  every data request behind them passes through `admit`.
- In-process peers (agent tools, workers) have no socket address and never reach the gate.
- The wrappers target the installed `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-connection` surface (verified against
  0.2.1-rc.3). An upstream rename fails activation instead of silently dropping the gate.

dsh-ip-based-acl README · Enforcement：A future `bypass` list — allowlisted peers that receive a browser session without a token — is not
implemented yet.

dsh-ip-based-acl README · Layout：| Path               | Purpose                                                                    |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `src/index.ts`     | Host plugin entry: `apply`, `inject`, re-exported `Config`, public seams    |
| `src/config.ts`    | `Config` schema (schemastery) and the `AclConfig` shape                    |
| `src/policy.ts`    | CIDR compilation, peer matching, and `X-Forwarded-For` resolution, framework-free |
| `src/gate.ts`      | Request-time gate over Connection's admission, index, and connect entries  |
| `test/`            | `node:test` suites run against `src/` through Node's type stripping        |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | Bundle patch: one `ip-based-acl` Host row                                  |
| `locale/en.json`   | Plugin Manager title and description                                       |
| `icon.svg`         | Original artwork exported as `./icon`                                      |
| `lib/`             | Build output (`pnpm build`); never edited by hand                          |
| `CONTRIBUTING.md`  | Setup, checks, commit rules, and how

dsh-ip-based-acl README · Commands：```sh
pnpm install      # dependencies
pnpm check        # typecheck + lint + format check + tests
pnpm build        # emit lib/index.js and lib/types/**.d.ts
pnpm dev          # tsc --watch on the build project

Node 24 or newer is required; tests run `test/**/*.test.ts` through native type stripping.

`lib/` is the published shape: `main`/`types` point into it, and `install_bundle` links the package
from a checkout, so run `pnpm build` before installing the bundle into a profile.

dsh-ip-based-acl README · Style：The conventions come from the author's reference TypeScript project and are enforced by the compiler,
ESLint, and Prettier rather than by review:

dsh-ip-based-acl README · Style：- `strict` plus `noUnusedLocals`, `noUnusedParameters`, `noImplicitReturns`, `noFallthroughCasesInSwitch`,
  `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `noImplicitOverride`.
- Double quotes, semicolons, trailing commas everywhere, 120-column lines, 2-space indentation.
- Type-aware ESLint (`projectService`) with `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` as a warning;
  `eslint-config-prettier` last so formatting stays Prettier's job.

Rules added for the Harness plugin layout:

dsh-ip-based-acl README · Style：- `erasableSyntaxOnly` — every source file must also run under Node's type stripping, which is how
  `pnpm test` executes `test/**/*.test.ts` against `src/` without a build step. No enums, namespaces,
  or parameter properties.
- `verbatimModuleSyntax` — type-only imports never leak into the emitted ESM.
- `rewriteRelativeImportExtensions` in the build project — source imports name `.ts` so the test
  runner can resolve them, and the emit rewrites them to `.js` for the published `lib/`.

dsh-ip-based-acl README · Harness contract：- The package is an ES module bundle: `dsh.bundle.patch` names `cordis.patch.yml`, whose single row
  carries the stable id `ip-based-acl`.
- The Host entry exports `apply(ctx, config)`, `Config`, and `inject: ["connection"]`; Cordis validates
  the row's `config` through the schema's Standard Schema interface before `apply` runs, and a profile
  without the `connection` service never applies the gate.
- Display metadata is exported without activating the plugin: `./locale/*.json` supplies
  `meta.title`/`meta.description`, `./icon` the artwork.
- Peer dependencies are the platform's: `@deepseek-ai/cordis` comes from the Harness install, while
  `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` is a real runtime dependency of this package.

dsh-ip-based-acl README · Verified：- `pnpm check` — typecheck, lint, formatting, and 32 policy and gate cases, including the trusted
  proxy walk, repeated headers, spoofed headers, and malformed entries.
- `pnpm build` — `lib/index.js` plus `lib/types/index.d.ts` in the layout `package.json` declares.

Not verified: installation into a live profile and the gate against a real browser session. The
unit tests exercise the wrappers with a stub Connection, not the shipped plugin.

dsh-ip-based-acl README · Contributing：Every commit must carry a [Developer Certificate of Origin](https://developercertificate.org/) sign-off,
so commit with `git commit --signoff` (`-s`). Git appends the trailer from your configured identity:

```
Signed-off-by: Your Name <you@example.com>
```

dsh-ip-based-acl README · Contributing：The trailer certifies the DCO 1.1 statement: you wrote the change, or you have the right to submit it
under the project's license, [AGPL-3.0-only](LICENSE). Do not type it by hand for work you did not
write, and do not drop it when rewriting or squashing commits.

[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) has the rest: local setup, the checks CI runs, and the commit
conventions. The DCO text itself is in [DCO](DCO).
